1. (Currently Amended) A method for restoring efficiency of a photovoltaic cell, the method comprising: illuminating a photovoltaic cell such that the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance equivalent to at least 5 hours of solar illumination at a solar intensity of approximately 1000 W/m²; and annealing the photovoltaic cell at a temperature above 90 degrees Celsius for a minimum of 10 minutes, wherein the annealing is performed in response to the illuminating step.

2. (Currently Amended) The method of Claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell comprises a semiconductor wafer, and wherein one of the following conditions is satisfied: the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance equivalent to at least 20 hours of solar illumination at a solar intensity of approximately 1000 W/m²; the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance equivalent to at least 16 hours of solar illumination at a solar intensity of approximately 1000 W/m² while the photovoltaic cell is heated to at least 50 degrees Celsius during the illuminating step; or the photovoltaic cell is irradiated in sunlight using a solar concentrator for at least 10 hours, wherein the solar concentrator increases the irradiance of solar illumination on the photovoltaic cell by a factor of 2 to 5.

3. (Currently Amended) The method of Claim 2, wherein the photovoltaic cell is annealed at a temperature above 130 degrees Celsius, and wherein the annealing step further comprises illuminating the photovoltaic cell simultaneously with the heating.

4. (Currently Amended) The method of Claim 3, wherein illuminating the photovoltaic cell during the annealing step is performed such that the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance equivalent to at least 10 minutes of solar illumination at a solar intensity of approximately 1000 W/m².

5. (Original) The method of Claim 1, wherein the semiconductor wafer is a silicon semiconductor wafer.

6. (Original) The method of Claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is annealed at a temperature between 140 degrees Celsius and 210 degrees Celsius for a minimum of 2 hours.

7. (Original) The method of Claim 6, wherein the photovoltaic cell is a thin film photovoltaic cell.

8. (Original) The method of Claim 6, wherein the photovoltaic cell is an amorphous silicon thin film photovoltaic cell.

9. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is illuminated after manufacturing of the photovoltaic cell is complete such that the photovoltaic cell produces electricity when illuminated.

10. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is illuminated with a light source that simulates light from the sun.
